skill.name: zarr-python
skill.description: Guides Python developers through Zarr chunked arrays, compression, cloud storage, parallel I/O, and integrations with NumPy, Dask, and Xarray.
skill.summary: Design efficient Zarr storage and processing workflows for large multidimensional arrays.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 90 static findings were adjudicated as false positives. Command alerts match Markdown fences, while URL alerts are documentation links; other alerts cite ordinary Zarr API and chunking text. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Use consolidated metadata to reduce latency: `zarr.consolidate_metadata(store)`
- Speeds up `tree()` operations and group traversal
- **Balance**: Larger chunks = fewer metadata operations; smaller chunks = better parallel access

content.value_statement: Large scientific arrays can overwhelm memory and storage systems. This skill guides chunking, compression, cloud storage, and parallel workflows with Zarr, NumPy, Dask, and Xarray.
actual_capabilities: Creates and opens chunked Zarr arrays with configurable shapes, data types, stores, and access modes.
Selects chunk shapes and sizes for row, column, random, and cloud access patterns.
Configures Blosc, Zstandard, Gzip, LZ4, and uncompressed storage options.
Uses local, memory, ZIP, S3, and Google Cloud Storage backends.
Integrates Zarr arrays with NumPy, Dask, and Xarray workflows.
Explains groups, attributes, metadata consolidation, sharding, resizing, appending, and synchronization.
limitations: The examples target Python 3.11 or later and may differ across Zarr versions.
Cloud examples require separately installed storage libraries and configured provider credentials.
The skill provides guidance but does not benchmark a dataset or select chunks automatically.
Concurrent writes still require careful chunk ownership or synchronization.

use_cases.title: Plan analytical data stores
use_cases.description: Design chunked local or cloud stores that support reliable ingestion and efficient downstream reads.

use_cases.title: Analyze multidimensional observations
use_cases.description: Store labeled climate or geospatial arrays for lazy analysis with Xarray and Dask.

use_cases.title: Modernize scientific formats
use_cases.description: Convert NumPy or HDF5 datasets into compressed Zarr stores for shared scientific workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a local array
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Zarr array for [shape], [data type], and [storage path]. Explain the chosen chunks, compression, and read and write operations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a local dataset

prompt_templates.title: Choose chunks and compression
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend chunks and compression for a [shape] array accessed mainly by [pattern]. Estimate chunk memory and explain the performance tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Performance planning for a known access pattern

prompt_templates.title: Design cloud storage
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Zarr workflow for [S3 or GCS] using [dataset size] and [worker count]. Include credential prerequisites, metadata consolidation, sharding, and concurrency controls.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a production pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Zarr pipeline: [description]. Identify memory, chunking, compression, metadata, and concurrent-write risks. Propose a prioritized optimization and validation plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a production workflow

output_examples.input: Store a 400 GB climate cube on S3 for daily time-slice reads.
output_examples.output: Use time-aligned chunks sized for cloud access. Enable compression, consolidate metadata after writes, and test representative reads before scaling.

output_examples.input: Reduce memory use while computing a mean over a large Zarr array.
output_examples.output: Open the store lazily with Dask. Keep chunks within worker memory and compute only the required reduction.

output_examples.input: Prepare several related arrays for fast browsing in one store.
output_examples.output: Organize arrays in groups, attach JSON-compatible attributes, and consolidate metadata after the hierarchy becomes stable.

best_practices: Base chunk shape on the most common read and write pattern, then validate it with representative workloads.
Keep each chunk and shard within available worker memory during compression and writes.
Consolidate metadata after structural changes, and refresh it before readers depend on the consolidated view.
anti_patterns: Do not load an entire large array into memory when chunked or lazy processing is available.
Do not allow multiple writers to update overlapping chunks without coordination.
Do not reuse one chunk layout for every access pattern or storage backend.

faq.question: Which storage backends are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers local directories, memory stores, ZIP files, Amazon S3, and Google Cloud Storage.

faq.question: How should I choose chunk sizes?
faq.answer: Start with the dominant access pattern and available memory. Then benchmark representative reads and writes before scaling.

faq.question: Does the skill manage cloud credentials?
faq.answer: No. Configure credentials through the selected storage library and cloud provider before opening a protected store.

faq.question: Can Zarr process data larger than memory?
faq.answer: Yes. Use chunked access or Dask lazy arrays so operations load only required chunks.

faq.question: Are concurrent writes automatically safe?
faq.answer: No. Coordinate overlapping writes with synchronization, or assign separate chunks to each writer.

faq.question: Will every example work with every Zarr version?
faq.answer: No. Confirm API compatibility with the installed version, especially for codecs, sharding, and synchronization.
